item.research_question: How do phase transformations, thermal expansion, and melting behavior manifest in five-component equimolar rare earth sesquioxide high-entropy alloys compared to their constituent pure oxides?
item.material_system: (La,Sm,Dy,Er,RE)2O3 where RE is Nd, Gd, or Y (HE-Nd, HE-Gd, HE-Y)
item.processing_route: Solution combustion synthesis followed by annealing at 800 °C for 96 h and 1100 °C for 12 h; laser melting using 400 W CO2 laser on copper hearth or in aerodynamic levitator; splat quenching with ~100 ms drop time; prolonged annealing at 800 °C for 60 days
item.test_conditions: Differential thermal analysis (DTA) in Ar flow at 20 °C/min up to 2500 °C; high-temperature synchrotron XRD (0.1236 Å wavelength) on laser-heated levitated samples (63–70 mg) with temperature monitoring via pyrometer (emissivity 0.92); room temperature XRD (40 kV, 40 mA, CuKα); electron microprobe analysis (WDS)
key_findings: All powders annealed at 800 °C contained mainly a C-type bixbyite structure with crystallite sizes of 20–40 nm.
Laser melting followed by splat quenching yielded a single-phase monoclinic B-type structure in all compositions.
Three reversible phase transitions were observed in the range 1900–2400 °C: B-A, A-H, and H-X.
The melting point of the (La,Sm,Dy,Er,Nd)2O3 sample was determined as 2456 ± 12 °C, which is higher than any constituent oxide.
Volume change on C-B transformation was calculated as ~8% in HE-Nd and HE-Gd samples.
Volume change on B-A transition was −2.5 ± 0.1% for HE-Nd and HE-Gd, and −3.1 ± 0.1% for HE-Y.
Volume change on H-X transformation was −1.2 ± 0.1% for HE-Nd and −0.6 ± 0.1% for HE-Y.
Average volume thermal expansion coefficient for the B-type structure was (3.5 ± 0.2) × 10−5/K.
item.mechanism: The increase in melting temperature is attributed to nonideal mixing in the solid and/or the melt, specifically negative deviations from ideality in the solid phase (local ordering) or positive deviations in the liquid phase, which favor the solid over the liquid.
item.limitations: Calphad predictions for the B-A transformation in HE-Y differed from experiments (predicted direct B-H transition); DTA sensor failure above 2300 °C limited enthalpy/entropy of fusion evaluation; XRD data quality did not allow unambiguous identification of the A-H transition; thermal gradients in laser-heated beads exceed 100 °C.
item.future_work: Future investigation of the liquidus surface in Sm2O3-Dy2O3, Sm2O3-Er2O3, and Dy2O3-Er2O3 systems is prompted to identify the source of the increased melting temperatures.
quotes: The melting point was determined for the (La,Sm,Dy,Er,Nd)2O3 sample as 2456 ± 12 °C, which is higher than for any of constituent oxides.

An increase in melting temperature is probably related to nonideal mixing in the solid and/or the melt and prompts future investigation of the liquidus surface in Sm2O3-Dy2O3, Sm2O3-Er2O3, and Dy2O3-Er2O3 systems.
Thermal analysis indicated three reversible phase transitions in the range 1900–2400 °C, assigned as transformations into A, H, and X rare earth sesquioxides structure types.
